abstract: Maintains environmental climate logs, desiccant cooling audits, and moisture stability reports
system_message:
You are Climate systems conservator (CLIM). The climate systems conservator (CLIM) oversees environmental monitoring for archival preservation vault facilities, maintaining microclimate telemetry logs, desiccant cooling performance audits, and relative humidity stability verification records across facility locations.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: United States·Maintains environmental climate logs, desiccant cooling audits, and moisture stability reports（FILTER）
information_points.content:
CLIM-FILTER-D3L：For the Laurentian Deep Geosphere Repository assessed under facility country United States, microclimate telemetry records indicate that validated relative humidity climate stability is false over the continuous 90-day test period.
CLIM-FILTER-X2L：Regarding the Scandinavian Permafrost Archive under facility country United States, microclimate audit records establish that validated relative humidity climate stability is false during the continuous 90-day test period.
CLIM-FILTER-8W7：Telemetry evaluations for the Bavarian Alpine Granite Vault under facility country United States demonstrate that validated relative humidity climate stability is true, maintaining the required 45% +/- 3% relative humidity through the continuous 90-day testing window.

information_points.title: Canada·Maintains environmental climate logs, desiccant cooling audits, and moisture stability reports（HVAC）
information_points.content:
CLIM-HVAC-OU9：Telemetry audits for the Scandinavian Permafrost Archive under facility country Canada indicate that validated relative humidity climate stability is false, having failed to sustain relative humidity within 45% +/- 3% across the continuous 90-day test period.
CLIM-HVAC-3IT：For the Laurentian Deep Geosphere Repository evaluated under facility country Canada, microclimate telemetry audits confirm that validated relative humidity climate stability is true, with relative humidity held within 45% +/- 3% during a continuous 90-day test period.
CLIM-HVAC-1L9：Continuous microclimate telemetry audits for the Bavarian Alpine Granite Vault under facility country Canada show that validated relative humidity climate stability is true, successfully maintaining relative humidity within 45% +/- 3% over the continuous 90-day test period.
